key_insight: The paper argues that language agents can learn better from intermediate steps, not just final outcomes, by co-training two complementary abilities: acting in the environment and forecasting what will happen next. This makes long-horizon agent training more efficient and uses supervision that standard RL usually ignores.
problem_solved: Training language agents is expensive because long rollouts are costly, and traditional reinforcement learning relies mainly on a single terminal reward. This leaves most intermediate-step supervision unused and makes it difficult to build good per-step learning targets.
method: Co-evolve two objectives during training: acting, which performs actions in the environment, and forecasting, which predicts future outcomes or responses.
Use intermediate supervision more effectively than terminal-only RL by turning step-level signals into learning targets for both action selection and prediction.
Reduce reliance on manually constructed value targets or environment-response targets, which are often hard to define accurately.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this approach offers a more sample-efficient way to train language agents on long-horizon tasks. It can improve learning from sparse rewards and may lead to more robust agents that better anticipate consequences before acting.

paper_title: Co-Evolving Acting and Forecasting for Language Agents
paper_authors: Haofei Yu, Yixing Chen, Yining Zhao, Xuyan Ye, Yuxiang Liu
